questions.q: What is a Git branch, really?
options: A full copy of all your files in a new folder
A name that points to one commit, and moves forward when you commit on it
questions.explain: A branch is just a label on a commit (a 41-byte file in .git). No files are copied, so branches are free.

questions.q: You are on main and run git switch -c diwali-sale. What happens?
options: A new branch diwali-sale is made on the current commit, and you move to it
Git makes a commit called diwali-sale
questions.explain: -c means create. Both main and diwali-sale point to the same commit; you are now on diwali-sale (the * in git branch).

questions.q: On diwali-sale, Neha commits sale.py. Where does main point now?
options: To the new commit, like diwali-sale
Still to the old commit: only the branch you are on moves
questions.explain: A commit moves only your current branch forward. That's how main stays safe while the sale is half-done.

questions.q: Neha switches from diwali-sale to main, and sale.py is gone from the folder. Why?
options: Git changed the folder to match main, which doesn't have sale.py. It is safe in the commit on diwali-sale
questions.explain: git switch updates your files to match the branch. Switch back to diwali-sale and sale.py returns.

questions.q: git switch main fails with: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by checkout. What should you do?
options: Commit the change (or stash or restore it), then switch
questions.explain: Git refuses so your uncommitted change isn't lost. Commit it on this branch, put it aside with git stash, or throw it away with git restore.

questions.q: Which command draws every branch and where they split?
questions.explain: --graph draws the lines, --all includes every branch (not only the one you're on), --oneline keeps one line per commit.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What does the file .git/refs/heads/main contain?
options: All the files of the main branch
The full hash of main's newest commit
questions.explain: A branch is a tiny file holding one 40-character commit hash. A commit on main overwrites it with the new hash.

questions.q: (Going deeper) git branch -d diwali-sale says: the branch 'diwali-sale' is not fully merged. What does it mean?
options: The branch has commits that are not in your current branch; deleting it could lose that work
You must be on diwali-sale to delete it
Git is out of disk space
questions.explain: -d only deletes branches whose commits are safe elsewhere. Merge it first (Lesson 3). -D would delete anyway, losing the work.
